# ngrrram

ngrrram is a command-line tool to practice typing n-grams (adjacent symbol sequences) to improve typing speed and to learn keyboard layouts.

A short showcase of the UI is available in the repository's assets.

Installation

- Precompiled releases are available for common platforms.
- Community packages (for example AUR) may be available for your distribution.

Usage

ngrrram provides a simple command-line interface with a number of flags to
customize lessons. Typical usage:

Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>    your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>   the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho         show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb               pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat                the most important flag. don\'t practice alone.
  -h, --help               Print help

Default recommended invocation:

  ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100

Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout you must specify both the input layout
(--emu-in) and the output layout (--emu-out). Supported layouts include:

- qwerty, qwertz, azerty, dvorak, colemak, colemakdh

Notes

- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of that lesson.
- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.

# ngrrram

`ngrrram` is a CLI tool to practice typing ngrams (`n` adjacent symbols in
particular order) to improve your typing speed and/or learn new keyboard
layouts effectively.

![a showcase of the ngrrram ui](./.github/showcase.gif)

Certain letter combination occur a lot more often than others, thus practicing
these in particular makes sense. This type of practice is often recommended for
example by [Ben Vallack](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sI-a64EVPPU) and Josh
Kaufman, who [learned Colemak in just 20 hours](https://first20hours.com)
making strong use of ngrams.

There already exists a good tool for this type of practice called
[ngram-type](https://github.com/ranelpadon/ngram-type). This tool is *heavily*
inspired by `ngram-type` and I want to thank Ranel Padon for creating it.

However, ngram-type does not support emulating different keyboard layouts,
which I found important so I would not have to switch my whole system to a
layout I was still learning.

Also, some people might prefer local/offline CLI based solutions over web based
ones.

## Installation

### Releases

Precompiled [releases](https://github.com/wintermute-cell/ngrrram/releases) for
linux, windows and macos are available.

### AUR (maintained by [JinEnMok](https://github.com/JinEnMok))

Use `yay` or any other AUR helper to install for an Archlinux system:

```bash
yay -S ngrrram-git
or
yay -S ngrrram-bin
```

### From Source

Make sure you have the rust tooling installed, then simply run:

```bash
cargo build --release
```

The executable will then be located at `./target/release/ngrrram`

### Looking for help packaging!

If you'd like to help by packaging for your platform, I'd gladly accept!

## Usage

`ngrrram` is not very complex. It offers a few customization options as command
flags, but starts with the recommended defaults if unconfigured.

Options:
```
Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>   your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>  the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho        show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb              pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat               the most important flag. don't practice alone.
  -h, --help              Print help
```

If you start `ngrrram` without parameters, it uses these recommended defaults:
```bash
ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100
```

## Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout in `ngrrram`, you must pass the flags
`--emu-in` and `--emu-out`, the first one describing your current layout, and
the second one being the one you want to emulate.

Available layouts are:

- `qwerty`    (Qwerty)
- `qwertz`    (Qwertz)
- `azerty`    (Azerty)
- `dvorak`    (Dvorak)
- `colemak`   (Colemak)
- `colemakdh` (ColemakDH)

> Having to provide an input layout is sub-optimal. I'm not sure how to get
> layout independent scancodes in rust; Could not get `device_query` to work.
> If you know a solution, please tell me.

## Random Notes
- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of
  that lesson; no need to stress.
- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.
  Otherwise WPM would unnaturally skyrocket with smaller ngrams.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Helper: run ./executable in tmux, feed keys with delays, capture screen."""
import subprocess, sys, time, os, re

def sh(*args, **kw):
    return subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, **kw)

class Session:
    def __init__(self, name="s", w=100, h=30, binary="./executable", args=None, cwd="/workspace"):
        sh("tmux","kill-server")
        time.sleep(0.4)
        self.name = name
        self.cwd = cwd
        sh("tmux","new-session","-d","-x",str(w),"-y",str(h),"-s",name,"bash")
        time.sleep(0.6)
        self.cmdline = binary + (" " + " ".join(args) if args else "")
        self.pipe = "/tmp/pipe_%s.log" % name
        try: os.remove(self.pipe)
        except OSError: pass
        sh("tmux","pipe-pane","-o","-t",name,"cat >> %s" % self.pipe)
        time.sleep(0.3)
        sh("tmux","send-keys","-t",name,self.cmdline)
        sh("tmux","send-keys","-t",name,"Enter")
    def keys(self, s, delay=0.06):
        sh("tmux","send-keys","-t",self.name,"-l",s)
        time.sleep(delay)
    def key(self, name, delay=0.06):
        sh("tmux","send-keys","-t",self.name,name)
        time.sleep(delay)
    def capture(self):
        r = sh("tmux","capture-pane","-t",self.name,"-p","-e")
        return r.stdout
    def capture_plain(self):
        return sh("tmux","capture-pane","-t",self.name,"-p").stdout
    def raw(self):
        try: return open(self.pipe,"rb").read()
        except OSError: return b""
    def close(self):
        sh("tmux","send-keys","-t",self.name,"Escape")
        time.sleep(0.5)
        sh("tmux","kill-server")
EOF

def split_frames(data: bytes):
    # frames separated by the "end of draw" marker
    marker = b'\x1b[39m\x1b[49m\x1b[59m\x1b[0m\x1b[?25h'
    parts = data.split(marker)

def readable(data: bytes):

    s = s.replace('\x1b[38;5;7m','[G7]').replace('\x1b[39m','[39]')
    s = s.replace('\x1b[1m','[B]').replace('\x1b[22m','[b]').replace('\x1b[3m','[I]').replace('\x1b[23m','[i]')
    s = s.replace('\x1b[38;5;2m','[GRN]').replace('\x1b[38;5;1m','[RED]').replace('\x1b[38;5;3m','[YEL]').replace('\x1b[38;5;4m','[BLU]').replace('\x1b[38;5;5m','[MAG]').replace('\x1b[38;5;6m','[CYA]')

    s = re.sub(r'\x1b\[(\d+);(\d+)H', r'@(\2,\1)', s)  # row;col -> (col,row)

import sys,time,re; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from run import Session
s=Session('a')
time.sleep(0.8)
def L():
    t=s.capture().split('\n')
    return (re.sub(r'\x1b','ESC',t[6])[1:-1],re.sub(r'\x1b','ESC',t[7])[1:-1],re.sub(r'\x1b','ESC',t[3]),re.sub(r'\x1b','ESC',t[16]),re.sub(r'\x1b','ESC',t[17]))
t0,b0,hdr,w1,w2=L()
lesson=re.sub(r'ESC\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]','',t0).strip()
print('lesson:',repr(lesson))
for ch in lesson+' ':
    s.keys(ch, delay=0.10)
    a,b,c,d,e=L()
    print('key %r -> %s | %s | %s | %s | %s'%(ch,a,b,c,d,e))
s.close()
"

print('\n'.join(kb()))

t0=s.capture().split('\n')[6]

print('lesson:',lesson)
s.keys('Z', delay=0.4); print('\n'.join(kb()))
print('=== after typing correct first char (%s) ==='%lesson[0])
s.keys(lesson[0], delay=0.4); print('\n'.join(kb()))
s.close()
""}

    s.close()
test(0.5); test(0.25); test(0.1)
EOF

import sys,time,re

# split into segments per escape

pos=(1,1)

    if m: pos=(int(m.group(2)),int(m.group(1))); continue
    if p.startswith('\x1b'): continue
    if p: out.append((pos,p))
    pos=(pos[0]+len(p),pos[1])
for pos,p in out: print(pos,repr(p))
s.close()
EOF

actions.command:
cd /workspace && python3 - <<'EOF'
import sys,time,re
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from run import *
def testemu(emu, phys):
    s=Session('a',args=emu+['-w','1','-a','0'])
    time.sleep(0.9)
    lesson=s.rows()[6][1:-1].strip()+' '
    print('emu=%r lesson=%r phys_keys_to_try=%r'%(emu,lesson,phys))
    for ch in phys:
        s.keys(ch,delay=0.12)
    rr=s.rows_raw()
    print('   tgt=',re.sub(r'\x1b','ESC',rr[6])[1:-1].strip())
    print('   ech=',repr(re.sub(r'\x1b','ESC',rr[7])[1:-1].strip()))
    print('   hdr=',strip_ansi(rr[3])[1:-1].strip())
    s.close()
testemu(['--emu-in','qwerty','--emu-out','colemak'],'kj kj kj kj kj kj ')
testemu(['--emu-in','qwertz','--emu-out','azerty'],'rq wr rq wr rq wr ')
EOF

EOF

cat <<'PYEOF' > /tmp/h/extract.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys, time, collections, threading, queue
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/h')
from term import App

def collect(narg, c, runs, top=200, extra=(), nthreads=6):
    out=[collections.Counter() for _ in range(nthreads)]
    def worker(tid, n):
        cnt=out[tid]
        for i in range(n):
            try:
                a=App(['-n',narg,'-c',str(c),'-r','1','-t',str(top),'-w','1','-a','0']+list(extra))
                a.wait(0.18)
                row=a.rows()[6][1:-1]
                a.close()
                for it in row.split(): cnt[it]+=1
            except Exception as e:
                pass
    ts=[]
    per=runs//nthreads
    for t in range(nthreads):
        th=threading.Thread(target=worker,args=(t,per)); th.start(); ts.append(th)
    for th in ts: th.join()
    total=collections.Counter()
    for c2 in out: total.update(c2)
    return total

if __name__=='__main__':
    narg=sys.argv[1]; runs=int(sys.argv[2]); c=int(sys.argv[3]); top=int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv)>4 else 200
    t0=time.time()
    cnt=collect(narg,c,runs,top)
    print('n=%s c=%d top=%d elapsed %.1f samples=%d unique=%d'%(narg,c,top,time.time()-t0,sum(cnt.values()),len(cnt)))
    import json
    json.dump(cnt.most_common(), open('/tmp/h/set_%s.json'%narg,'w'))
    print('saved')
PYEOF

EOF

import sys,time,re
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/h')
from term import App
def get(a,rowi=17):
    r=a.rows()[rowi][1:78]

def getw(a):
    r=a.rows()[16][1:78]
    m=re.search(r'avg\.\s*(\d+)WPM,\s*last\s*(\d+)WPM',r); return (int(m.group(1)),int(m.group(2))) if m else None

        if i in errs:
            a.send('z' if ch!='z' else 'q'); time.sleep(delay)

        a.send(ch); time.sleep(delay)

    type_lesson(a, lesson, (1,)); a.wait(0.2)
    print('after lesson %d: acc avg=%d wpm=%r'%(li,get(a),getw(a)))
a.close()
EOF

```rust
pub fn diff<'a>(&self, other: &'a Self) -> Vec<(u16, u16, &'a Cell)> {
    let previous_buffer = &self.content;
    let next_buffer = &other.content;
    let mut updates: vec = vec![];
    // Cells with an invalid character should not be drawn
    let mut invalidated: usize = 0;
    let mut to_skip: usize = 0;
    for (i, (current, previous)) in next_buffer.iter().zip(previous_buffer.iter()).enumerate() {
        if !current.skip && (current != previous || invalidated > 0) && to_skip == 0 {
            let (x, y) = self.pos_of(i);
            updates.push((x, y, &next_buffer[i]));
        }
        to_skip = current.symbol().width().saturating_sub(1);
        let affected_width = std::cmp::max(current.symbol().width(), previous.symbol().width());
        invalidated = std::cmp::max(affected_width, invalidated).saturating_sub(1);
    }
    updates
}
```

```rust
    let mut updates: vec = vec![];
```

```
fn complete(&mut self) {
    let elapsed = start.elapsed();  // from the first keystroke
    let words = nonspace_chars(lesson) as f64 / 5.0;
    let wpm = if elapsed_secs > 0 { (words * 60.0 / elapsed_secs) as u32 } else { u32::MAX };

    let success = wpm >= wpm_threshold && acc >= acc_threshold;
    if success { ok_count += 1 } else { bad_count += 1 }

    last_acc = acc; acc_sum += acc; acc_count += 1;
    lesson_num += 1;
    new_lesson();
}
```

```rust
pub fn diff<'a>(&self, other: &'a Self) -> Vec<(u16, u16, &'a Cell)> {
    let previous_buffer = &self.content;
    let next_buffer = &other.content;
    let mut updates: vec = vec![];
    // Cells with an invalid character should not be drawn
    let mut invalidated: usize = 0;
    let mut to_skip: usize = 0;
    for (i, (current, previous)) in next_buffer.iter().zip(previous_buffer.iter()).enumerate() {
        if !current.skip && (current != previous || invalidated > 0) && to_skip == 0 {
            let (x, y) = self.pos_of(i);
            updates.push((x, y, &next_buffer[i]));
        }
        to_skip = current.symbol().width().saturating_sub(1);
        let affected_width = std::cmp::max(current.symbol().width(), previous.symbol().width());
        invalidated = std::cmp::max(affected_width, invalidated).saturating_sub(1);
    }
    updates
}
```

```rust
pub fn generic_jaro<'a, 'b, Iter1, Iter2, Elem1, Elem2>(a: &'a Iter1, b: &'b Iter2) -> f64 {
    let a_len = a.len(); let b_len = b.len();
    if a_len == 0 && b_len == 0 { return 1.0; }
    else if a_len == 0 || b_len == 0 { return 0.0; }
    else if a_len == 1 && b_len == 1 { return if a[0]==b[0] {1.0} else {0.0}; }
    let search_range = (max(a_len,b_len) / 2).saturating_sub(1);
    let mut b_consumed = vec![false; b_len];
    let mut matches = 0.0;
    let mut transpositions = 0.0;
    let mut b_match_index = 0;
    for (i, a_elem) in a.enumerate() {
        let min_bound = if i > search_range { max(0, i - search_range) } else { 0 };
        let max_bound = min(b_len - 1, i + search_range);
        if min_bound > max_bound { continue; }
        for (j, b_elem) in b.enumerate() {
            if j < min_bound { continue; }
            if j > max_bound { break; }
            if a_elem == b_elem && !b_consumed[j] {
                b_consumed[j] = true;
                matches += 1.0;
                if j < b_match_index { transpositions += 1.0; }
                b_match_index = j;
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    if matches == 0.0 { 0.0 } else {
        (1.0/3.0) * ((matches / a_len as f64) + (matches / b_len as f64) + ((matches - transpositions) / matches))
    }
}
```

```rust
pub fn generic_jaro<'a, 'b, Iter1, Iter2, Elem1, Elem2>(a: &'a Iter1, b: &'b Iter2) -> f64 {
    let a_len = a.len(); let b_len = b.len();
    if a_len == 0 && b_len == 0 { return 1.0; }
    else if a_len == 0 || b_len == 0 { return 0.0; }
    else if a_len == 1 && b_len == 1 { return if a[0]==b[0] {1.0} else {0.0}; }
    let search_range = (max(a_len,b_len) / 2).saturating_sub(1);
    let mut b_consumed = vec![false; b_len];
    let mut matches = 0.0;
    let mut transpositions = 0.0;
    let mut b_match_index = 0;
    for (i, a_elem) in a.enumerate() {
        let min_bound = if i > search_range { max(0, i - search_range) } else { 0 };
        let max_bound = min(b_len - 1, i + search_range);
        if min_bound > max_bound { continue; }
        for (j, b_elem) in b.enumerate() {
            if j < min_bound { continue; }
            if j > max_bound { break; }
            if a_elem == b_elem && !b_consumed[j] {
                b_consumed[j] = true;
                matches += 1.0;
                if j < b_match_index { transpositions += 1.0; }
                b_match_index = j;
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    if matches == 0.0 { 0.0 } else {
        (1.0/3.0) * ((matches / a_len as f64) + (matches / b_len as f64) + ((matches - transpositions) / matches))
    }
}
```
